issues.legal_issue: A possession clause in a consent decree is not penal where it grants the tenant a concession against execution if the tenant pays all dues by the deadline, and the decree is executable when the tenant fails to meet that condition.
material_facts: The eviction suit was settled by a consent decree requiring the tenant to deliver possession and pay the amounts due by a specified deadline.
The decree provided that the landlord would not execute the possession decree if the tenant paid all arrears and other specified amounts by that deadline.
The tenant paid only part of the amount due and failed to pay the entire amount by the deadline.
issues.conclusion: The non-execution clause was a concession, not a penalty. Because the tenant did not satisfy its condition, the possession decree was executable and the matter was remitted to the executing court to proceed in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: A clause is penal when it imposes a consequence for failure to comply; a clause that gives a benefit for timely compliance is a concession. The character of a consent decree depends on the dispute and the court's role in approving it. Applying section 12(3) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, and Order XXI Rule 35 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the Court held that failure to satisfy the condition for the concession made the possession decree executable. No earlier case was relied on for this conclusion.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_execution and consent_decree_awards_possession and landlord_promises_nonexecution_if_all_dues_paid_by_deadline and tenant_fails_to_pay_all_dues_by_deadline

predicates.rent_control_eviction_execution: The proceeding seeks to execute a possession decree arising from an eviction dispute governed by rent-control law.
predicates.consent_decree_awards_possession: The parties' consent decree requires the tenant to deliver possession and pay amounts due.
predicates.landlord_promises_nonexecution_if_all_du: The landlord agrees not to execute the possession decree if the tenant pays all specified dues by a deadline.
predicates.tenant_fails_to_pay_all_dues_by_deadline: The tenant does not pay all specified dues by the deadline.

issues.definition: When a rent-control eviction execution involves a consent decree awarding possession, a landlord's conditional promise not to execute, and the tenant's failure to pay all dues by the deadline, the possession decree is executable.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant in an eviction case governed by rent-control legislation cannot obtain relief against forfeiture under the general forfeiture provision when the governing rent-control legislation supplies the applicable conditions for protection from eviction.
material_facts: The eviction suit was brought under the rent-control legislation for arrears of rent.
The tenant had failed to pay or tender the rent and permitted increases required for protection from eviction.
The tenant sought to resist execution by relying on the general forfeiture-relief provision of the Transfer of Property Act.
issues.conclusion: The case had to be resolved under section 12(3) of the rent-control legislation, not section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act; the tenant could not obtain the additional protection of section 114.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, is a special provision that incorporates the equity of section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, in modified form. A tenant governed by the rent-control legislation must meet its requirements and cannot claim double protection under section 114. The Court relied on Pradesh Kumar Bajpai v. Binod Behari Sharkar and distinguished the reliance placed on Krishnabai v. Hari and Gajanand Govind v. Pandurang Keshav.

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns eviction governed by rent-control legislation.
predicates.tenant_fails_to_meet_statutory_rent_cond: The tenant does not satisfy the rent-payment or tender requirements for protection from eviction under the governing legislation.

issues.definition: When an eviction proceeding is governed by rent-control legislation and the tenant fails to meet its rent-related conditions, general forfeiture relief is unavailable.
